softened.title: Softened Butter/Cream Cheese
softened.description: Leave at room temperature for 30-45 minutes until easily dented with finger but not melting. Or microwave in 10-second intervals, checking frequently.

room temp.title: Room Temperature Eggs
room temp.description: Place eggs in warm water for 5-10 minutes, or leave on counter 30 minutes before use. Cold eggs can cause butter to seize in creamed mixtures.

warm to 43°C.title: Warm Liquid for Yeast
warm to 43°C.description: Heat to 40-46°C (105-115°F). Too hot kills yeast, too cold won't activate. Should feel warm but not hot on wrist — like a comfortable bath.

bloomed.title: Blooming Yeast
bloomed.description: Dissolve yeast in warm liquid with a pinch of sugar. Wait 5-10 minutes until foamy. If no foam, yeast is dead — start with fresh yeast.

packed.title: Packed Brown Sugar
packed.description: Press brown sugar firmly into measuring cup until compact. Level off top. Properly packed sugar holds its shape when dumped out.

sifted.title: Sifted Flour/Sugar
sifted.description: Pass through fine-mesh sieve to remove lumps and aerate. Especially important for confectioners' sugar in glazes to prevent graininess.

melted.title: Melted Butter
melted.description: Melt in microwave in 30-second intervals or in small saucepan over low heat. For 'melted and cooled', let sit 5-10 minutes until warm but not hot.

diced.title: Diced Butter (Cold)
diced.description: Cut cold butter into 1cm cubes. Keep refrigerated until needed. Cold butter creates flaky layers in pastry as it melts during baking.
